subject.title: [Bug]: CLI relay exits silently with code 1 when session lane is blocked — no timeout or busy error surfaced

question: Should Gateway-backed CLI same-session lane waits become a terminal structured busy result, and should that result use a distinct exit code?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the permanent CLI contract affects orchestration scripts and message-delivery semantics beyond a mechanical stderr rendering fix.

options.title: Structured Busy Result
options.body: Return a CLI-visible lane-busy error with wait details after the configured wait threshold and document the selected exit-code behavior.

options.title: Timeout Message Only
options.body: Keep queued execution semantics unchanged and only render the existing timeout/failure path with clearer stderr output.

options.title: Defer Contract
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers settle whether terminal busy rejection should be default behavior or opt-in.

recommendation.title: Structured Busy Result
recommendation.body: Return a CLI-visible lane-busy error with wait details after the configured wait threshold and document the selected exit-code behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The Gateway-backed CLI relay and surrounding queue/Gateway history point to this owner as the best routing candidate for the CLI contract decision.
